item.description:
Last authors: Ferenc Borondics, Francesco Capitani

Authors: Bastien Michon, Yingpeng Yu, Beatrice D'Alò, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Electronic structure and metallic transition in the high-interest bilayer nickelate superconductor.

Tags: #nickelate #superconductivity #material

Abstract: Here, the authors map the temperature-pressure evolution of the bilayer nickelate La 3 Ni 2 O 7 and reveal that the suppression of tilts in oxygen octahedra is accompanied by a pronounced crossover toward a higher-carrier-density metallic state. By establishing the structural phase boundary over a broad temperature-pressure range, their results highlight the intimate interplay between lattice structure and electronic properties in this novel high-T c superconductor.

item.title: [9] Observation of subharmonic charge-density-wave correlations in La-based cuprates
item.description:
Last authors: M. Fujita, C.-C. Kao

Authors: J.-S. Lee, S. A. Kivelson, H. Lee, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Soft X-ray scattering on CDW and PDW correlations in cuprates; directly matches spectroscopic interests.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #CDW #cuprate #superconductivity

Abstract: Suggestive but indirect evidence for pair-density-wave correlations has been reported in several high- T c cuprates, yet a bulk-sensitive scattering signature of the expected subharmonic charge response has remained elusive. Here, the authors use resonant soft x-ray scattering to identify a reproducible subharmonic charge density wave response near half the primary charge-ordering wave vector in two La-based cuprates. The response emerges in the stripe-ordered, layer-decoupled superconducting regime, where charge, spin, and superconducting correlations are intertwined.

item.title: [8] Spin-Hall angle temperature dependence in NiFe/MnBi2Te4 heterostructures
item.description:
Last authors: A. I. Chernov, K. A. Zvezdin

Authors: A. S. Pakhomov, V. V. Yurlov, P. N. Skirdkov, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study on MnBi2Te4, a core topological material relevant to user's magnetic interest.

Tags: #topological #heterostructure #spintronics

Abstract: Pairing a ferromagnet with the MnBi 2 Te 4 offers a promising route to efficient spin-to-charge conversion, but how well it performs across temperature had remained unmapped. Combining ferromagnetic resonance with inverse spin-Hall voltage measurements from 20–290 K, the authors show here that the spin-Hall angle stays nearly constant below approximately 130 K, then becomes unreliable as spin rectification and shifting damping take over. The results establish the material as a robust platform for cryogenic spin-orbit and topological spintronics.
